full_judgment:
3. Defendant-appellants contested the suit. Their case was that the suit land is part of CS Plot No. 3271 of mouza Hogla which consists of 21.61 acres of land out of which the plaintiff claimed only one acre. The rent receiving interest of the Zamindars were acquired under Chapter II and the entire CS plot was acquired by the Government as the same was under the khas possession of the ex-landlord. The plaintiff has no possession and the suit is liable to be dismissed The case of defendants No. 2-3 was that they took pattan of 3 acres of land out of the suit Dag No. 3271 and they are in possession on payment of Government rent. H is stated that the plaintiff himself also prayed for taking pattan of a portion of the land but since he was not in possession his prayer was not granted by the Government. 

 10. In MH Khandakar vs Bangladesh DLR (SC) 1 this Court explained the meaning of 'raiyat' and "tenant" and it was pointed out that a tenant of an agricultural holding is generally called 'raiyat'. Further it was observed that the main object of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was to eliminate all those interests intervening between the Government and the tenant in actual occupation of land to create, throughout the country, one class of tenants directly under the Government, which would be the sole receiver of rent payable by the tenants in rested of the lands comprised in their tenancy and their rights and liabilities would be regulated by uniform code of laws. In the present case the rent-receiving interests were acquired by the Government, since the Zamindar was replaced by the Government. And the tenant, the respondent, intended to pay rent to the Government and went to do so to the Tahsil Office; it was not accepted. But he is on the land-it is only one acre out of 21 acres. He even wanted to take pattan from the Government. His tenancy light has matured over the last forty years to his status. It was only against the ex-landlord that he took the plea of adverse possession as abundant caution. In so far as the Government, his new land- lord, is concerned, he was willing to pay rent and continue to do so. Payment of arrear rent is subject to law. His status however cannot be denied.
